name: Morning 5
rules: Barefoot, every morning, right after waking. Half-hearted counts.
No pain, no forcing end range: move to a comfortable stretch, breathe, come back.
If you only have 2 minutes: do steps 1, 3 and 6.

steps.dose: 5 × 5 s per foot, seated or standing
steps.why: Pull the ball of the foot toward the heel without curling the toes, lifting the arch. Directly trains the small arch muscles that flat feet underuse. Meta-analysis shows a real but small effect on navicular drop.

steps.dose: 10 reps: big toe up / others down, then switch
steps.why: Restores independent toe control, which the tripod foot needs to grip the ground.

steps.drill: The Screw hold in ready position
steps.why: Rotate both feet outward into the floor without moving them: the arch rises, glutes fire, knees line up. Installs the flat-foot correction you'll use in every standing lift and sport.
Ankle dorsiflexion is usually limited with flat feet and causes knees to cave. Rocking the knee over the 2nd toe toward the wall restores range under control.
Rotates both hips through internal and external rotation; moving actively through the range builds ROM similarly to stretching (Afonso 2021).

steps.dose: 5 per side, breathe out as you open
steps.why: A stiff upper back forces the shoulders and arm to rotate alone, feeding arm-first sequencing. Opening the thoracic spine lets the trunk rotate as one link in the chain.

steps.dose: 5 breaths: 4 s in through nose, 6-8 s out
steps.why: Long exhales shift the nervous system out of the protective, grip-everything state, which is part of why you feel stiff everywhere.

teachMe: Your stiffness is partly protection: the brain limits range when it doesn't trust the base (collapsed arches) or senses threat. These 5 minutes give it a stable foot, a reminder that each joint can move safely, and a calm breath, so it gradually loosens the brake. Strength through full range builds mobility about as well as stretching (Afonso 2021), so your loaded lifts keep this going all day.
